narrative.intro: Applied Research Solutions has federal contract obligations of $236M in FY2026 to date. Applied Research Solutions received 7 awards so far this fiscal year, and the average award size is $33.7M. Applied Research Solutions saw obligations down 11.5% year over year. Applied Research Solutions has a strong concentration in defense work: the Department of Defense accounted for $230M of obligations in FY2026 to date. Applied Research Solutions sells research and engineering services, with Research and Development in the Physical, Engineering, and Life Sciences (except Biotechnology) totaling $217M and related research categories adding $11.9M. Applied Research Solutions has smaller obligations from the General Services Administration, which contributed $6.4M. Applied Research Solutions recorded multi-year variation in receipts, with fiscal-year obligations ranging from $207M in FY21 to $267M in FY25 before the $236M reported in FY26. Applied Research Solutions’ portfolio shows large, concentrated awards and a handful of buyers driving most of the current-year obligations.

sections.heading: How concentrated are Applied Research Solutions' customers?
sections.body: The Department of Defense is the dominant buyer for Applied Research Solutions, with obligations of $230M in FY2026 to date. The General Services Administration is a distant second with $6.4M. The heavy DoD concentration means a small number of buyers account for most revenue. The company received 7 awards in the current fiscal year, which supports that concentration.

sections.heading: What are Applied Research Solutions' primary products and markets?
sections.body: Research and Development in the Physical, Engineering, and Life Sciences (except Biotechnology) is the largest market for Applied Research Solutions at $217M. Applied Research Solutions also has work in Research and Development in the Physical, Engineering, and Life Sciences (except Nanotechnology and Biotechnology) at $11.9M and Engineering Services at $6.4M. Smaller obligations include Process, Physical Distribution, and Logistics Consulting Services at $921K. Those markets align with the large DoD obligations reported in FY2026 to date.

faq.q: How much does Applied Research Solutions make from federal contracts?
faq.a: Applied Research Solutions has federal contract obligations of $236M in FY2026 to date. Applied Research Solutions received 7 awards this fiscal year and the average award size is $33.7M. Applied Research Solutions obligations are down 11.5% year over year.

faq.q: Which agencies buy from Applied Research Solutions?
faq.a: The Department of Defense buys the most from Applied Research Solutions, obligating $230M in FY2026 to date. The General Services Administration is the other listed buyer, obligating $6.4M.

faq.q: What does Applied Research Solutions sell to the government?
faq.a: Applied Research Solutions sells research and engineering services to the government, led by Research and Development in the Physical, Engineering, and Life Sciences (except Biotechnology) at $217M. Applied Research Solutions also sells related R&D and Engineering Services, including $11.9M in Research and Development in the Physical, Engineering, and Life Sciences (except Nanotechnology and Biotechnology) and $6.4M in Engineering Services, plus $921K in Process, Physical Distribution, and Logistics Consulting Services.
